title: Python coap/gateway test suite has ~1212 pre-existing failures on beads-worker-4 post-main-merge
description: Found while verifying worker6-tm4o/nb3f constant consolidation (2026-09-09). On beads-worker-4 at 5c00afccf3+ (after merging 264 commits from main), running: uv run --directory python pytest tests/announce tests/coap tests/gateway ... yields 1212 failed / 1336 passed. Verified IDENTICAL failure count with the constant-consolidation changes stashed (clean tree) — failures are pre-existing, not caused by consolidation. Failure clusters: coap/test_sqlite_store.py (36), test_sos_resource.py (67+), test_messages_resource.py (90+), test_resource_directory.py (48+), test_edhoc_responder.py (27), test_secure_lifecycle.py (27), gateway/test_ble_lci.py (BLE on headless box), plus ~24 collection errors from missing dev deps (jsonschema/httpx/hypothesis — cf. k9xb). Needs triage: are these missing-dev-deps fallout, genuinely red from the 264-commit merge, or a broken uv sync env on this host? Discovered-from: project-LICHEN-worker6-nb3f
close_reason:
TRIAGE COMPLETE — root cause: incomplete uv sync (missing 'dev' extra), NOT a red merge. The dev deps (jsonschema/httpx/hypothesis) are declared as the [project.optional-dependencies] dev extra and locked in uv.lock, but this host's .venv had been synced WITHOUT --extra dev, producing ~24 collection errors that cascaded into ~1211 of the ~1212 reported failures.

FIX APPLIED (environment repair, no repo change needed): cd python && uv sync --extra dev. This is already the documented invocation (python/README.md:18, docs/renode-workflow.md:471); the gap was environment state, not docs.

VERIFICATION: uv run pytest tests/announce tests/coap tests/gateway -q => 2510 passed, 5 skipped, 3 xfailed, 1 intermittent (was ~1212 failed). All bead-named clusters now green: test_sqlite_store, test_sos_resource, test_messages_resource, test_resource_directory, test_secure_lifecycle, test_edhoc_responder (38/38 standalone), test_ble_lci (10/10 — bleak present; earlier 'headless BLE' note was actually collection-error cascade, not real hardware failure). The 264-commit merge from main is NOT red.

RESIDUAL (filed, not fixed — OSCORE-adjacent/human-only): 1 order-dependent flake test_edhoc_responder.py::TestEdhocResource::test_restart_m1_is_rejected_and_original_can_complete — passes standalone (1/1) and with its file alone (38/38), fails only in full-suite ordering. Distinct mechanism (test-isolation leak, not wall-clock) from up5p; evidence added as comment on project-LICHEN-worker6-up5p.

No source/test files modified; nothing to codereview. .venv change is untracked+gitignored.
